name: Bali
description: Everyone ends up here. The question is which part you actually want to be in.
detail: Ubud, Seminyak, Canggu — same island, totally different trips. Most people pick wrong the first time.

neighbourhoods.name: Ubud
neighbourhoods.vibe: Rice field treks, spiritual temples & jungle retreats
tips: Walk Tegallalang rice terraces before 8am — after that it's tour groups
Avoid staying on Monkey Forest Road itself — too loud at night

neighbourhoods.name: Seminyak
neighbourhoods.vibe: Boutique hotels, sunset beach bars & rooftop dining
tips: Merah Putih restaurant for a proper Balinese meal in a beautiful space
The beach faces west — sunset here is worth doing once

neighbourhoods.name: Canggu
neighbourhoods.vibe: Surf breaks, co-working cafés & the creative scene
tips: Old Man's beach bar is the social hub, good for meeting people
Rent a motorbike rather than taxis — it's how everyone gets around

name: Paris
description: Lived in or visited — Paris feels completely different depending on where you stay.
detail: Le Marais has a completely different energy from Montmartre. Same city, two different trips.

neighbourhoods.name: Le Marais
neighbourhoods.vibe: Art galleries, Jewish quarter, vibrant nightlife & the best falafel
tips: L'As du Fallafel on Rue des Rosiers is the real thing — eat it standing on the street
Visit weekdays; weekend crowds in the Marais are brutal

neighbourhoods.name: Saint-Germain
neighbourhoods.vibe: Classic cafés, independent boutiques & literary history
tips: Café de Flore is for tourists; Café Procope on Rue de l'Ancienne Comédie is the real one
Luxembourg Gardens are quieter than Tuileries and nicer to sit in

neighbourhoods.name: Montmartre
neighbourhoods.vibe: Cobblestones, Sacré-Cœur & sweeping city panoramas
tips: Avoid restaurants immediately around Sacré-Cœur — walk two blocks south for actual Parisian prices
Best view of Paris is from Square Louise Michel, not the basilica steps

name: Tokyo
description: Overwhelming at first. Then you find your neighbourhood and the whole city clicks.
detail: No two districts feel alike. Shinjuku and Yanaka could be different cities entirely.

neighbourhoods.name: Shinjuku
neighbourhoods.vibe: City pulse, neon-lit alleys, izakayas & the main transit hub
tips: Golden Gai has ~200 tiny bars — just pick one that looks interesting and walk in
East side (Golden Gai) and west side (Omoide Yokocho) feel completely different — both worth a night

neighbourhoods.name: Shibuya
neighbourhoods.vibe: Iconic crossing, youth fashion, department stores & live music
tips: The famous crossing is best from the Starbucks window above — less chaotic, better photos
Yoyogi Park is 10 minutes from Harajuku station; go Sunday afternoon

neighbourhoods.name: Yanaka
neighbourhoods.vibe: Old Tokyo charm, temple streets & handmade artisan shops
tips: Yanaka Ginza shopping street is one of the few places in Tokyo that feels pre-war
The cemetery here is surprisingly beautiful and worth walking through

name: New York
description: Picking the wrong neighbourhood here costs you an hour each way, every day.
detail: Midtown is convenient and soulless. Brooklyn is worth the subway. You need to pick before you book.

neighbourhoods.name: Midtown
neighbourhoods.vibe: Central Park, Times Square, skyscraper views & everything in reach
tips: Stay here if you need to — but eat elsewhere. Walk to Hell's Kitchen for real food
The High Line is most enjoyable 7–9am before it fills up

neighbourhoods.name: Williamsburg
neighbourhoods.vibe: Brooklyn creative hub, rooftop bars, record stores & great food
tips: Take the L train from Manhattan — 15 minutes and a completely different city
Walk north toward Greenpoint from Bedford Ave for fewer tourists

neighbourhoods.name: Lower East Side
neighbourhoods.vibe: Downtown edge, vintage clothing, late-night venues & culture
tips: Russ & Daughters on Houston St for bagels — the original, not the cafe version
Most bars don't get going until midnight. Plan accordingly.

name: Santorini
description: Tiny island. Huge price range. Where you stay changes everything about the experience.
detail: Oia gets the photos. Fira has the restaurants. Imerovigli has the quiet. You can't have all three.

neighbourhoods.name: Oia
neighbourhoods.vibe: Blue-domed churches, cliffside walks & the best sunsets on Earth
tips: Book sunset restaurants at least a week ahead — everyone is trying to eat at the same time
Walk the path from Fira to Oia (10km) — the best views are along the way, not just at the end

neighbourhoods.name: Fira
neighbourhoods.vibe: The main town — restaurants, nightlife & unbroken caldera views
tips: Better for nightlife and eating than Oia — far fewer tourists staying here
The cable car down to the old port is fine; the donkeys are faster but be prepared

neighbourhoods.name: Imerovigli
neighbourhoods.vibe: Quietest spot, highest ridge & the most dramatic scenery
tips: Skaros Rock walk starts here — 45 minutes return, no crowds, best caldera view on the island
Quietest of the three main towns; restaurants are mostly hotel-only which is a disadvantage

name: Dubai
description: Sky-high ambition and ancient souks in the same taxi ride. Stranger than it sounds.
detail: Downtown Dubai and Al Fahidi feel like different centuries. Both are worth your time — but not from the same hotel.

neighbourhoods.name: Downtown
neighbourhoods.vibe: Burj Khalifa, Dubai Mall, fountain shows & luxury hotels
tips: Book Burj Khalifa observation deck online in advance — the in-person queue is hours long
Dubai Fountain show is free and runs every 30 minutes after 6pm

neighbourhoods.name: Jumeirah Beach
neighbourhoods.vibe: Beachfront resorts, watersports, open sea & white sand
tips: Public beach at JBR Walk is free — no need to pay for a hotel beach
Walk The Walk outdoor mall for evening dining — cooler than going inside

neighbourhoods.name: Al Fahidi
neighbourhoods.vibe: Historic wind towers, traditional souks & authentic old Dubai
tips: The Dubai Museum is one of the cheapest and best in the city
Take an Abra (wooden boat) across the Creek for 1 AED — one of the best things in Dubai

name: Machu Picchu
description: Getting there is half the trip. Most people don't plan that part properly.
detail: You need to acclimatise before you ascend. Cusco is non-negotiable. The trek or the train — that's your real first choice.

neighbourhoods.name: Aguas Calientes
neighbourhoods.vibe: Gateway base town, hot springs, jungle market & easy citadel access
tips: Book the bus to the ruins in advance — the 4am queue is long enough without waiting for tickets
Train from Cusco to here is the experience; don't take the bus option

neighbourhoods.name: Inca Trail
neighbourhoods.vibe: 4-day classic trek through mountain cloud forest & ancient ruins
tips: Permits sell out months in advance — book before you book your flights
Day 2 is the hardest. Day 3 through the Sun Gate is the payoff.

neighbourhoods.name: Cusco
neighbourhoods.vibe: Inca stonework, colonial plazas, altitude acclimatisation & great dining
tips: Spend at least 2 nights acclimatising before attempting altitude hikes
San Pedro Market is for locals; Mercado Central is for tourists — both worth visiting

name: Sydney
description: Bondi is just the postcard. There's a whole other city behind it worth exploring.
detail: Circular Quay has the views. Bondi has the beach. Surry Hills has the restaurants worth lining up for.

neighbourhoods.name: Circular Quay
neighbourhoods.vibe: Opera House steps, Harbour Bridge views & ferry connections everywhere
tips: The Manly ferry is the best $5 you'll spend — 30 minutes of harbour views
Opera House tours are worth it; the building is better inside than outside

neighbourhoods.name: Bondi Beach
neighbourhoods.vibe: Surf culture, the coastal walk, weekend markets & all-day café life
tips: Walk the coastal path to Bronte and Coogee — far less crowded than Bondi Beach
Icebergs pool is a Sydney institution; swim early morning for the full experience

neighbourhoods.name: Surry Hills
neighbourhoods.vibe: Indie restaurants, craft bars, gallery spaces & the local scene
tips: Crown Street has the best independent coffee and food in Sydney
Bills on Crown Street for breakfast — the ricotta pancakes are exactly what people say they are

name: Rome
description: Overrun, overpriced in parts, and still one of the best cities on earth.
detail: Two thousand years of history on a street you walked to get coffee. Pick the wrong neighbourhood and you're paying tourist prices for everything.

neighbourhoods.name: Trastevere
neighbourhoods.vibe: Evening restaurants, ivy-covered walls, local market & no chain stores
tips: Eat before 7:30pm or after 9pm to avoid the tourist dinner rush completely
Da Enzo al 29 — cash only, no reservations, queue outside. Worth it.

neighbourhoods.name: Prati
neighbourhoods.vibe: Quiet residential blocks near the Vatican, good food, few tourists
tips: Best gelato in Rome: Fatamorgana on Via Laurina — unusual flavours done properly
Walk to Castel Sant'Angelo along the river at sunset — almost nobody does this

neighbourhoods.name: Testaccio
neighbourhoods.vibe: The original Rome — the market, meat-heavy food culture & proper locals
tips: Flavio al Velavevodetto for cacio e pepe — not tourist-facing, proper Roman trattoria
The non-Catholic cemetery here has Keats and Shelley's graves and is unexpectedly beautiful

name: Barcelona
description: Beach city with a food scene serious enough that the beach almost becomes secondary.
detail: Don't stay in the Gothic Quarter for a week. It's for day trips. The rest of the city is where the actual Barcelona is.

neighbourhoods.name: Eixample
neighbourhoods.vibe: Gaudí buildings, wide avenues, the main restaurant scene & good transport
tips: Cervecería Catalana on Mallorca Street for the best pintxos in the city
Book Sagrada Família weeks ahead — the ticket queue is not something you want to experience

neighbourhoods.name: Gràcia
neighbourhoods.vibe: Bohemian, local, summer fiestas & completely away from the tourist track
tips: Plaça del Sol for evening aperitivo — sit on the steps with locals
The Gràcia Festival in August turns the entire neighbourhood into a street party

neighbourhoods.name: Barceloneta
neighbourhoods.vibe: Beach neighbourhood, seafood, crowded in summer but still worth it
tips: El Vaso de Oro — tiny standing bar on Carrer de Balboa. Order the beer and anything fried.
Get there by 10am in summer. By 11am the beach is a wall-to-wall crowd.

name: Amsterdam
description: Smaller than people expect. More interesting than the reputation suggests.
detail: The canal ring is beautiful. The Jordaan has the best independent shops in the city. The museums are world-class. Most people spend the whole trip in a three-block radius.

neighbourhoods.name: Jordaan
neighbourhoods.vibe: Narrow canals, independent galleries, the best cafés & weekly markets
tips: Winkel 43 for the apple pie — eat it warm with cream outside on the canal
Anne Frank House tickets sell out 2+ months ahead; book the moment you know your dates

neighbourhoods.name: De Pijp
neighbourhoods.vibe: The local choice — Albert Cuyp market, Indonesian food & good bars
tips: Saturday Albert Cuyp Market for street food — best in the city
Brouwerij 't IJ craft brewery is in an actual working windmill

neighbourhoods.name: Oud-West
neighbourhoods.vibe: Residential, creative, and the version of Amsterdam that locals actually live in

name: Singapore
description: The city that proves efficiency and character aren't mutually exclusive.
detail: Expensive by Southeast Asia standards but also completely different from the rest of it. The hawker centres alone are worth the flight.

neighbourhoods.name: Marina Bay
neighbourhoods.vibe: Skyline views, the spectacle and luxury that genuinely delivers

neighbourhoods.name: Tiong Bahru
neighbourhoods.vibe: Singapore's oldest estate — independent bookshops, excellent coffee

neighbourhoods.name: Little India
neighbourhoods.vibe: The most sensory neighbourhood, cheap hawker food & completely different energy

name: Bangkok
description: Chaotic, loud, brilliant. The food will ruin every Thai restaurant back home.
detail: Sukhumvit for convenience, Rattanakosin for the temples, Ari for the locals. The traffic is bad but the BTS skytrain means you rarely need a taxi.

neighbourhoods.name: Sukhumvit
neighbourhoods.vibe: Expat hub, BTS access, international restaurants & busy nightlife
tips: Terminal 21 mall food court for cheap, actually good food — ignore the shopping
Thonglor and Ekkamai (BTS stops past Asok) are where the real Bangkok nightlife is

neighbourhoods.name: Rattanakosin
neighbourhoods.vibe: Historic island, temples, the river & the old backpacker scene

neighbourhoods.name: Ari
neighbourhoods.vibe: Residential, the Bangkok that locals actually use — good for a slower week

name: Kyoto
description: Tokyo has momentum. Kyoto makes you actually stop and look.
detail: Visit in spring for cherry blossoms or autumn for the maples. Avoid Golden Week. The city rewards slow walking — rent a bicycle and get into the backstreets.

neighbourhoods.name: Higashiyama
neighbourhoods.vibe: Temple district, preserved machiya townhouses & scenic evening walks
tips: Most temples charge ¥500–700 entry — budget that into the day
Walk the Philosopher's Path north to south in cherry blossom season — first week of April

neighbourhoods.name: Gion
neighbourhoods.vibe: Geisha district, traditional teahouses — best on weekday evenings
tips: Hanamikoji Street on a Tuesday or Wednesday evening — geisha visible around 6pm
Don't photograph geisha without permission or try to stop them for photos

neighbourhoods.name: Arashiyama
neighbourhoods.vibe: Bamboo grove, riverside temples & worth the 25-minute train from center
tips: Bamboo Grove is best at 7am before tour groups arrive. After 9am it's crowded regardless.
Tenryu-ji garden is worth the extra ¥500 for the sub-garden — one of the best in Japan

name: Reykjavik
description: The whole country is the attraction. The city is just where you start.
detail: Northern lights from October to March. Midnight sun in summer. Waterfalls and geysers within two hours of the city. Book the car, not just the hotel.

neighbourhoods.name: 101 Reykjavik
neighbourhoods.vibe: The center — everything walkable, the bar scene & Hallgrímskirkja church
tips: The hot dog stand by the harbour (Bæjarins Beztu) — cash only, been there since 1937
Laugavegur Street for everything in the evening — eat at Snaps bistro for local fish

neighbourhoods.name: Grandi
neighbourhoods.vibe: Harbor district, fish and chips, whale watching & the Viking World museum
tips: Sægreifinn (Sea Baron) for the best lobster soup in Iceland for about $10
Whale watching from the Old Harbour — book Elding tours, most reliable operators

neighbourhoods.name: Laugardalur
neighbourhoods.vibe: East of center, the geothermal pool complex & quieter residential streets
tips: Laugardalslaug public pool — huge thermal complex for about $9, where Icelanders actually swim
Árbær Open Air Museum gives real context for how Icelanders lived 100 years ago

name: Buenos Aires
description: Steak, tango, and a European city accidentally in South America.
detail: Flights are expensive but once you land everything else isn't. Dinner starts at 10pm. The wine is better and cheaper than anywhere. Stay at least ten days.

neighbourhoods.name: Palermo
neighbourhoods.vibe: Parks, brunch culture, design boutiques and the main nightlife zone
tips: Don Julio parrilla for steak — arrive when it opens at noon to avoid the 2-hour queue
Rent a bike from the Palermo Chico cycle stations for the parks

neighbourhoods.name: San Telmo
neighbourhoods.vibe: Antiques market, tango shows, colonial buildings and Sunday feria
tips: Sunday Feria de San Telmo market — go early before 11am
Bar Sur on Estados Unidos for tango — small, authentic, not a show for tourists

neighbourhoods.name: Recoleta
neighbourhoods.vibe: Elegant boulevards, French architecture, the cemetery and old money energy
tips: The cemetery is free and takes 2 hours to walk properly — Evita's tomb is well-signposted
La Biela café across from the cemetery has been serving coffee for 70+ years

name: Tbilisi
description: A city that rewards the people who bother to show up. Most don't.
detail: Wine, sulphur baths, Soviet brutalism next to medieval churches. The old town feels like it hasn't been renovated for tourism yet — and that's exactly the point.

neighbourhoods.name: Old Town (Abanot-ubani)
neighbourhoods.vibe: Sulphur baths, balconied houses & the authentic Tbilisi atmosphere
tips: Sulphur baths in Abanotubani — Chreli Abano is the best value public bath at about $5
Walk up to Narikala Fortress in the evening for the best view over the city

neighbourhoods.name: Fabrika
neighbourhoods.vibe: Repurposed Soviet factory, boutiques, craft bars & creative coworking
tips: Good for coffee in the morning, cocktails in the evening — the courtyard fills after 8pm
The hostel inside is one of the best in the city even if you're not staying there

neighbourhoods.name: Vera
neighbourhoods.vibe: Tree-lined streets, local cafés, less tourist-facing and genuinely residential
tips: Entree restaurant on Tsereteli Ave — Georgian food done properly without tourist markup
The Botanical Garden is a 20-minute walk from Fabrika through the old town

name: Medellín
description: The transformation story is real. More importantly, the city is just good now.
detail: Cable cars to hilltop neighbourhoods. A metro that actually works. Street food that costs less than your morning coffee back home. Come for a week, stay considerably longer.

neighbourhoods.name: El Poblado
neighbourhoods.vibe: Expat hub, restaurants and nightlife — comfortable but not cheap for Colombia
tips: Pergamino for the best coffee in the city — Colombian beans done properly
Parque Lleras fills after 10pm — the surrounding streets have better bars with fewer tourists

neighbourhoods.name: Laureles
neighbourhoods.vibe: Local neighbourhood feel, better value, great cycling infrastructure
tips: Better local food and about 30% cheaper than El Poblado for accommodation
Ruta N area for coworking and speciality coffee if you're working remotely

neighbourhoods.name: La Candelaria
neighbourhoods.vibe: Historic centre, street art, slightly rough around the edges, properly local
tips: Take the Metrocable to Comunas 13 for street art — go with a guide, not solo
Plaza Botero has the famous Botero sculptures and is completely free

name: Porto
description: Better than Lisbon for most trips and half the price. Don't tell everyone.
detail: Azulejo tiles, river views, port wine cellars, and steep streets that make you work for the view. Smaller than Lisbon, easier to get around, and still genuinely affordable.

neighbourhoods.name: Ribeira
neighbourhoods.vibe: UNESCO waterfront, wine bars and the classic postcard view from Dom Luís Bridge
tips: Tasca do Chico for fado — tiny, book in advance, one of the last authentic fado restaurants in Portugal
Walk across Dom Luís Bridge to Vila Nova de Gaia for port wine tasting — the cellars are free to tour

neighbourhoods.name: Bonfim
neighbourhoods.vibe: The real Porto — locals, indie shops, not a tourist trap
tips: Mercado do Bolhão for produce and local life — better than any tourist market
Cantina 32 for creative Portuguese food at reasonable prices

neighbourhoods.name: Foz do Douro
neighbourhoods.vibe: Where the river meets the sea, residential and calm
tips: Matosinhos is a 30-minute walk along the coast — best grilled fish restaurants in the region
Sunset at the Atlantic from Praia de Matosinhos is one of the best in Portugal

name: Chiang Mai
description: Bangkok gets the bookings. Chiang Mai gets the return visits.
detail: 300 temples, night markets, mountains within an hour, and a cost of living that makes it the de facto base for Southeast Asia slow travel. Cooler and calmer than the south.

neighbourhoods.name: Old City
neighbourhoods.vibe: Moat-surrounded historic core, temples at every corner, guesthouses and cafés
tips: Warorot Market (Kad Luang) for local produce and cheap textiles — better value than the Night Bazaar
A cooking class here is worth half a day — pick one that visits the market first

neighbourhoods.name: Nimman
neighbourhoods.vibe: The creative quarter — coffee culture, boutique shops, co-working
tips: Ristr8to espresso bar for the coffee — obsessive about quality, small menu
Maya Mall rooftop at sunset before hitting the bars on the lower floors

neighbourhoods.name: Riverside
neighbourhoods.vibe: Laid back, good food, less touristy and cooler in the evenings
tips: Long boat tours along the Ping River run until dark and cost about $3
The Good View restaurant — order the sai ua (northern sausage)

name: Sarajevo
description: The most underestimated city in Europe. Not for long.
detail: East meets West in the most literal sense — Ottoman bazaars give way to Austro-Hungarian architecture on the same street. Excellent food, almost no queues, and hotels that would cost four times as much in Prague.

neighbourhoods.name: Baščaršija
neighbourhoods.vibe: Ottoman old bazaar, coppersmith streets and the beating cultural heart of the city
tips: Ćevapi at Petica — the original spot, one of the oldest restaurants in the city
Walk across the Latin Bridge — this is where Franz Ferdinand was assassinated in 1914

neighbourhoods.name: Grbavica
neighbourhoods.vibe: Post-war residential quarter, lived-in feel and away from tourist circuits
tips: Klub Kulture Kriterion is the best bar in the city — in a renovated cinema
Kibe Mahala neighbourhood market on Saturday mornings — all local, no tourists

neighbourhoods.name: Ilidža
neighbourhoods.vibe: Green spa suburb, hot springs, tram ride from centre
tips: Vrelo Bosne park — the spring source of the Bosna river, rent a horse-drawn carriage
Terme Federal Hotel spa is open to non-guests for day use — thermal pools at low prices

name: Oaxaca
description: Every food person you know has been here. They're not wrong.
detail: Mezcal, mole negro, tlayudas, and some of the most distinct regional craft in Mexico. The historic centre is genuinely walkable and the surrounding valley has enough to fill two weeks without repeating yourself.

neighbourhoods.name: Centro Histórico
neighbourhoods.vibe: Colonial zócalo, colourful facades, markets and the main cultural strip
tips: Mercado 20 de Noviembre for tlayudas and memelas — eat at the market, not the surrounding restaurants
Museo de las Culturas de Oaxaca inside the Santo Domingo complex is free and genuinely excellent

neighbourhoods.name: Jalatlaco
neighbourhoods.vibe: Quiet cobblestoned barrio, boutique stays and excellent breakfast spots
tips: Casa Oaxaca restaurant — book ahead and eat on the terrace
Best visited at 7am before tour groups arrive from the hotels

neighbourhoods.name: Xochimilco
neighbourhoods.vibe: Local barrio, few tourists, traditional food and authentic neighbourhood life
tips: El Pochote organic market on Fridays for the best produce in the city
Local mezcal bars here charge local prices — half what you'd pay in Centro

name: Plovdiv
description: Older than Athens, quieter than anywhere, and €10 dinners with wine.
detail: Seven hills, a Roman amphitheatre still used for concerts, and an old town that looks like it was painted by someone with too much talent. The rest of Europe hasn't caught up yet.

neighbourhoods.name: Old Town (Staría Grad)
neighbourhoods.vibe: National Revival architecture, galleries, art studios and the hilltop panorama
tips: Visit during the Lampartite light festival in December — the whole old town becomes a gallery
The Kapana (the Trap) creative quarter is separate from the Old Town but a 5-minute walk

neighbourhoods.name: Kapana
neighbourhoods.vibe: The Trap — creative district, street art, independent bars and restaurants
tips: Bar 4 on Bratya Pulevi for natural wine — small bar, excellent selection, no tourist pricing
Friday and Saturday evenings the whole district comes alive — skip it during the day, go at night

neighbourhoods.name: Kършияка
neighbourhoods.vibe: Residential northern bank, local market, none of the tourist surcharge
tips: Trud Market on Saturday mornings for produce and secondhand finds
Café One for breakfast — run by locals, prices haven't changed in years

name: Kotor
description: A walled medieval city that costs a third of Dubrovnik and is half as crowded.
detail: Bay of Kotor, stone streets, cats everywhere by local tradition, and fortress walls you can walk. Base here and day-trip the rest of the Adriatic coast without the cruise ship crowds.

neighbourhoods.name: Stari Grad (Old Town)
neighbourhoods.vibe: Walled city, medieval churches, narrow alleys and the main social scene
tips: Walk the fortress walls in the early morning — 1,300 steps but the views are worth every one
Konoba Cattaro on Trg od Salate for grilled fish — inside the walls, no tourist markup

neighbourhoods.name: Dobrota
neighbourhoods.vibe: Bayside village just north of the walls, calm, local and half the price
tips: Stari Mlini restaurant right on the water — one of the best meals in Montenegro for reasonable money
Rent a car or scooter — the bay road north toward Perast is one of the most beautiful drives in the Adriatic

neighbourhoods.name: Prčanj
neighbourhoods.vibe: Quietest stretch of the bay, baroque mansions and very few other travellers
tips: Gospa od Anđela church dates to 1420 — almost never has visitors despite being remarkable
Swim from the rocks below the main road — clear water and usually empty in early morning

name: Budapest
description: The ruin bars alone are worth the flight. Everything else is a bonus.
detail: Two cities separated by the Danube. Buda is quiet and hilly. Pest is where everything happens. The thermal baths work out to about the price of a coffee back home.

neighbourhoods.name: District VII (Jewish Quarter)
neighbourhoods.vibe: Ruin bars, the old ghetto, best nightlife in Central Europe
tips: Szimpla Kert is the original ruin bar and still the best — go on Sunday for the farmers market inside
Kadár étkezde on Klauzál Square for authentic Jewish-Hungarian lunch — no dinner service, cash only

neighbourhoods.name: Buda Castle District
neighbourhoods.vibe: History on a hill, panoramic views over the Danube and zero nightlife
tips: Visit the castle on a Monday when most museums in Pest are closed
The funicular up from Clark Ádám Square costs about $5 — not necessary but a nice way up

neighbourhoods.name: District IX (Ferencváros)
neighbourhoods.vibe: Emerging neighbourhood, cheaper accommodation and a young creative scene
tips: Bálna Budapest cultural centre for views over the Danube — go for the terrace, skip the restaurant
Hold Utca Market Hall for the freshest produce with far fewer tourists than the Great Market Hall

name: Hoi An
description: The lanterns are real. The tailors are real. The crowds are real too — go early.
detail: Get a suit or dress made in 24 hours for less than you'd spend on a takeaway at home. The ancient town is genuinely beautiful at night. The beach is 4km away.

neighbourhoods.name: Ancient Town
neighbourhoods.vibe: UNESCO lantern-lit streets, tailors and the main scene — worth the crowds
tips: Go at dawn — by 9am it's shoulder-to-shoulder. The lanterns are lit regardless of the hour.
Get measured for custom clothing on Day 1 — 24-hour turnaround but you'll want fitting time

neighbourhoods.name: An Bang Beach
neighbourhoods.vibe: 4km from town, good seafood, expat-friendly and quieter than Da Nang
tips: Soul Kitchen beach club for sunset — better food and more relaxed than the Ancient Town restaurants
Bike from the Ancient Town in 20 minutes along the river road

neighbourhoods.name: Cam Nam Island
neighbourhoods.vibe: Local island across the footbridge, almost no tourists and good food stalls
tips: Cross the footbridge at the south end of the Ancient Town — 5-minute walk to a completely different world
Morning market on the island runs until 8am — some of the cheapest local food in the area

name: Mexico City
description: One of the greatest food cities in the world. It took a while for people to notice.
detail: Roma Norte has the restaurant scene. The historic centre has Aztec ruins under colonial buildings. The altitude hits harder than expected. Everything costs less than you think.

neighbourhoods.name: Roma Norte
neighbourhoods.vibe: Tree-lined streets, design hotels, the best restaurant scene in the country
tips: Contramar for fish — queue or book, do not skip it
Walk Álvaro Obregón avenue in the evening for the best people watching and street food

neighbourhoods.name: Condesa
neighbourhoods.vibe: Art deco apartments, parks, dog walkers and a more residential feel
tips: Parque México is the social hub — sit, eat, watch people walk their dogs
El Parnita for weekend brunch — local crowd, no tourists, excellent mezcal selection

neighbourhoods.name: Centro Histórico
neighbourhoods.vibe: Aztec ruins beneath colonial buildings — overwhelming, essential and cheap
tips: Palacio de Bellas Artes free entry Sunday mornings — Diego Rivera murals inside worth seeing alone
Café de Tacuba on Tacuba Street — founded 1912, still using the original recipes

name: Cartagena
description: The walled city is as good as the photos. The neighbourhood next to it is better.
detail: Walk the wall at sunset. Eat in Getsemaní. Take a boat to the Rosario Islands. Don't stay in Bocagrande unless you want a beach holiday with none of the character.

neighbourhoods.name: Ciudad Amurallada
neighbourhoods.vibe: The walled colonial centre, the postcard — and the heat
tips: La Cevichería for ceviche — small, book ahead, the best in the city by some distance
Walk the walls at sunset: start from Baluarte de San Francisco Javier and walk the full circuit

neighbourhoods.name: Getsemaní
neighbourhoods.vibe: Murals everywhere, the better bars, cheaper food and a neighbourhood with actual life
tips: El Santísimo for cocktails — the neighbourhood's best bar, always full after 9pm
La Movida street food from vendors in Parque Getsemaní after 7pm — cheaper and better than most restaurants

neighbourhoods.name: Bocagrande
neighbourhoods.vibe: Beach suburb, mostly for families and Colombian tourists — skip unless that's you
tips: Skip it unless you specifically want a beach resort vibe far from the city's character
If you do go, the beach at Laguito is better than the main Bocagrande strip

name: Split
description: People actually live inside a Roman palace. That's not a metaphor.
detail: Diocletian's Palace is a UNESCO site where people have apartments and hang their laundry. Base here and island-hop without Dubrovnik's prices and cruise ship crowds.

neighbourhoods.name: Diocletian's Palace
neighbourhoods.vibe: Living inside Roman walls — apartments, restaurants and centuries of overlap
tips: The basement halls (entrance from Peristyle) are free and mostly ignored by tourists
Eat at Fife on Trogirska Street — cash only, standing room only at lunch, genuinely local

neighbourhoods.name: Bačvice
neighbourhoods.vibe: Beach bar district, the local sport of picigin and the summer social scene
tips: Picigin — the local beach ball game is played here every morning. Join in if you want.
The bars close around 1am and the beach stays busy until then in summer

neighbourhoods.name: Varoš
neighbourhoods.vibe: Old stone quarter behind the palace, quiet, local and the best hidden dining
tips: Stari Grad restaurant on Aljinovića for Dalmatian food without the palace premium
The highest point gives views over the palace rooftops — unmarked path, worth finding

name: Valletta
description: The entire capital is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It's also the smallest in the EU.
detail: Cross it end to end in 20 minutes. Every building has a story going back 500 years. Flights are cheap from most of Europe and the food has improved dramatically in the last decade.

neighbourhoods.name: Valletta Proper
neighbourhoods.vibe: The whole city is walkable — grand baroque buildings at every corner
tips: Upper Barrakka Gardens for the 12 noon cannon firing — free, spectacular, takes 2 minutes
Trabuxu Bistro in Strait Street for the best wine list in Malta

neighbourhoods.name: Sliema
neighbourhoods.vibe: Modern waterfront, shopping, sea swimming and the practical base for day trips
tips: Exiles Beach for swimming — concrete lido, free to use, far better than any paid beach
Walk one block inland from The Strand restaurants for local prices

neighbourhoods.name: Marsaxlokk
neighbourhoods.vibe: Southern fishing village, Sunday market and the freshest seafood on the island
tips: Sunday market starts at 7am and winds down by 10am — don't arrive after that
Ir-Rizzu restaurant right on the harbour for the freshest fish on the island

name: Yogyakarta
description: Borobudur is 45 minutes away. That's already a reason to come.
detail: Bali gets all the tourists. Yogyakarta gets the travellers. The sultan's palace, the silver workshops, the shadow puppet performances, and the volcano you can climb — all for a fraction of Bali's prices.

neighbourhoods.name: Kraton (Palace Quarter)
neighbourhoods.vibe: The sultan's palace complex, batik workshops and traditional shadow puppets
tips: The palace interior has restricted access — the outer grounds are free and worth an hour
Batik workshops on Jalan Tirtodipuran: watch the process and buy direct from the maker

neighbourhoods.name: Prawirotaman
neighbourhoods.vibe: Art district, boutique guesthouses, good food and a slower pace
tips: ViaVia café is the neighbourhood hub — good food, notice board for local events and tours
Most guesthouses here will organise a driver to Borobudur for sunrise — book the night before

neighbourhoods.name: Kota Gede
neighbourhoods.vibe: Old silver town, Mataram ruins and traditional craft workshops
tips: Silver workshops still do everything by hand — you can watch the process for free and buy at source
The old royal cemetery at Imogiri is 20 minutes south and rarely visited

name: Riga
description: The world's largest collection of Art Nouveau buildings. Almost nobody knows this.
detail: Medieval old town, Soviet-era market halls, Art Nouveau streets, and a food scene that's been quietly excellent for years. Cheaper than Tallinn, more interesting than Vilnius. The locals will debate this.

neighbourhoods.name: Old Town (Vecrīga)
neighbourhoods.vibe: Medieval streets, the best-preserved old city in the Baltics
tips: Ēdnīca Lāčplēsis on Lāčplēša iela for Latvian home-style food at Soviet cafeteria prices — it's excellent
St. Peter's Church tower for the best views over the old town — lift costs €9

neighbourhoods.name: Art Nouveau District
neighbourhoods.vibe: Alberta iela and the surrounding streets — architecture unlike anywhere else in Europe
tips: The Art Nouveau Museum at Alberta 12 shows the interiors — mandatory if you're walking the street
Most buildings are still residential — ring the bell on any unlocked door to look at the entrance halls

neighbourhoods.name: Ķīpsala
neighbourhoods.vibe: Island suburb across the Daugava river, quiet, local and great river views
tips: Walk across the Vanšu Bridge and follow the river embankment — quiet, local, tourist-free
Lido at Ķīpsala is the largest Latvian food hall in the country — cheap, excellent, open all day

name: Lisbon
description: Everyone arrives expecting a city. They find a series of villages that happen to be next to each other.
detail: Seven hills, tram 28, half the price of Barcelona. Alfama for fado and history, Bairro Alto for nights that start at midnight, Belém for the things you have to see once. The food is better than people expect and the coffee is among the best in Europe.

neighbourhoods.name: Alfama
neighbourhoods.vibe: The old Moorish quarter — steep, labyrinthine, fado coming through restaurant doors after dark
tips: Take tram 28 through — the whole route costs €3 and is the best tour of the city
Fado at Tasca do Chico: small, authentic, book weeks ahead

neighbourhoods.name: Bairro Alto
neighbourhoods.vibe: Students, bars, restaurants packed on narrow streets — the city's nightlife centre since the 1980s
tips: Cervejaria da Trindade for craft beer in a 13th-century convent — one of the strangest and best bars in Portugal
Eat before 10pm if you want a seat without queuing

neighbourhoods.name: Belém
neighbourhoods.vibe: Pastéis de Belém, Jerónimos Monastery, the Monument to the Discoveries — all within a 10-minute walk
tips: Pastéis de Belém: the original, the recipe is secret, the queue moves fast — order six
Jerónimos Monastery is free on Sunday mornings before 2pm

name: Hanoi
description: Louder, faster, and more interesting than people expect. The old town is still actually old.
detail: The French Quarter, the Old Quarter, and West Lake are three completely different cities side by side. Street food here is better than anywhere in Vietnam. The chaos makes sense after two days — cross the road slowly and confidently, the scooters will flow around you.

neighbourhoods.name: Old Quarter
neighbourhoods.vibe: 36 traditional guild streets, each originally selling one thing — still mostly true today
tips: Bún chả at Bún Chả Hương Liên — the place Obama ate. It's genuinely worth it.
Street addresses in the Old Quarter are often wrong — navigate by landmark and phone

neighbourhoods.name: French Quarter
neighbourhoods.vibe: Wide boulevards, colonial architecture, better restaurants and Hoan Kiem Lake at the centre
tips: Long Train Street — coffee bars appeared for the spectacle of trains passing 30cm from tables
KOTO restaurant for Vietnamese food with a social enterprise element — good cause, better food

neighbourhoods.name: Tay Ho (West Lake)
neighbourhoods.vibe: Quieter residential neighbourhood around the lake — best coffee in the city, expat community
tips: Cafe Giang on Nguyen Huu Huan for egg coffee — invented here in the 1940s
Cycle around the lake in early morning before the city wakes up

name: Cape Town
description: The most dramatically beautiful city most people underestimate until they arrive.
detail: The mountain, the ocean, the winelands 45 minutes away, and a food scene that has quietly become one of the best on the continent. The neighbourhoods are as different as cities. Stay in the City Bowl if you want everything walkable; Sea Point if you want the Atlantic on your doorstep.

neighbourhoods.name: City Bowl
neighbourhoods.vibe: The centre below Table Mountain — cafés, galleries, the Company's Garden, base for everything
tips: Truth Coffee Brewing on Buitenkant St — extreme coffee obsessives, excellent
Walk up Lion's Head at sunrise — 2 hours, no guide needed, views that rival Table Mountain

neighbourhoods.name: De Waterkant
neighbourhoods.vibe: Cobblestone streets, boutique hotels, Cape Quarter market — the best-kept neighbourhood secret
tips: Biscuit Mill in Woodstock (10 mins away) for the Saturday market — the city's best food market
The Waterfront is the tourist thing; De Waterkant is where Cape Town actually eats and drinks

neighbourhoods.name: Sea Point
neighbourhoods.vibe: Atlantic seaboard promenade — free tidal pools, local restaurants, better value than the Waterfront
tips: Olympic Pool at Sea Point Pavilion — 50m outdoor pool on the Atlantic for about $3
La Perla on Beach Road for calamari and wine on the terrace — been there since 1952

name: Lima
description: The best food city in South America. It's not close.
detail: Ceviche, tiradito, causa, anticuchos — the street food alone justifies the flight. Barranco has the best nightlife and the most interesting streets. Most people stay in Miraflores because it's convenient and miss what makes Lima worth going to. At least eat in Barranco.

neighbourhoods.name: Barranco
neighbourhoods.vibe: Artist's neighbourhood on the Pacific cliffs — bohemian bars, murals, the Bridge of Sighs
tips: Central restaurant (usually on the world's best restaurant lists) — book months ahead
La Noche bar on Bolognesi Street for live music after 10pm — the neighbourhood's institution

neighbourhoods.name: Miraflores
neighbourhoods.vibe: Safe, convenient, pleasant and slightly soulless — good base, not the real Lima
tips: Huaca Pucllana — a real Inca pyramid in the middle of a suburb, lit up at night
Larcomar mall is worth visiting for the Pacific cliff views — the mall itself is irrelevant

neighbourhoods.name: Surquillo
neighbourhoods.vibe: The local market district — where Lima's chefs actually shop, no tourist markup
tips: Mercado N°1 de Surquillo: buy ceviche ingredients from the same stalls the chefs use
Isolina on Av. San Martín for criollo cooking — less glamorous than Central, just as good
